summary: Iter 66 re-run of AGOP-D wellness language lock after the two-layer post-filter (clarity_safety.py) was added. 8/8 tests pass on first run, 8/8 on second run, and a 6x stress repeat against the two most adversarial cabinet prompts found ZERO banned words across all replies. The legal-safety lock is now AIRTIGHT under the founder-enumerated banned-word set. Smoke regressions (neutral 'tired tonight', 'shoulders heavy') still produce non-empty replies with valid tone_tag. Open Factory + Realtime gating unchanged: /api/clarity/access returns has_active_pass:true / tier:'free_access', /api/clarity/realtime/health returns enabled:false / has_openai_key:false.

minor.issue: Cosmetic grammar artifact from Layer 1 substitution: Claude wrote 'any diagnosis or treatment plan' and the regex rewrote it to 'any a naming or a plan with a licensed practitioner' — the leading 'any' collides with the inserted article, yielding 'any a naming'. Not a clinical leak (no banned word), but reads awkwardly. Consider adding a Layer-1 post-pass that strips 'any a ' -> 'any ' and 'any an ' -> 'any '. Same fix can collapse 'a a' / 'an a' that already has handling but does not catch determiner+article collisions like 'any a', 'some a', 'this a'.

action_items: OPTIONAL (cosmetic only) — Polish clarity_safety.py Layer 1 to also collapse 'any a / any an / some a / this a / that a' article collisions left over after substitutions like 'diagnosis' -> 'a naming'.

OPTIONAL — Consider adding 'bipolar' and 'psychiatrist' to the AGOP-D explicit example list inside the system prompts (they ARE handled by clarity_safety.py Layer 1 already, but adding to the prompt would reduce Layer 2's nuclear-fallback firing rate).
critical_code_review_comments: clarity_safety.py is well-designed: Layer 1 is grammar-aware (handles article 'a/an', specific phrases like 'panic disorder' before standalone 'disorder'), and Layer 2 is the hard nuclear option (canned _SAFE_FALLBACK). Idempotent. Good separation.
Layer 2's _HARD_BANNED regex covers every founder-enumerated banned word from the iter-66 spec — verified by reading list against BANNED_PHRASES in the test file.

clarity_ai._split_signals applies sanitize_reply() as the final step before returning — confirmed at line 679-682 with a defensive try/except so the filter is best-effort and never breaks the conversation. body_room_ai.py reuses _split_signals from clarity_ai, so the same filter runs in both rooms — single point of truth.

Iter-65's three CRITICAL leaks ('treatment'/'therapist'/'psychiatrist' in cabinet PTSD reply; 'diagnose'/'trauma' in body_room traumatized reply; 'diagnosis' in body_room anxiety-disorder reply) are now ALL fixed. The Layer 1 substitutions catch the prompt's own redirect templates that previously contradicted the banned-word list.
Smoke regressions are unchanged: neutral replies still flow naturally, tone_tag remains in the valid set, AGOP-A pacing holds. The filter does not regress non-clinical conversation.

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8) over two consecutive runs + 6x stress repeat (12/12 zero-banned)

rca of the issue: Iter 65 RCA was self-contradicting prompts (banned-word list vs redirect-template instruction inside the same prompt). Iter 66 fix is structural and the correct move: a hard post-LLM regex filter that runs on every mentor reply regardless of what the prompt or the model decided to say. Layer 1 does grammar-aware substitution (preserving readability); Layer 2 falls back to a safe canned reply if any banned token survives. Idempotent. Best-effort wrapped in try/except so it never breaks the chat. Same filter is shared across rooms via clarity_ai._split_signals.
